title: Installer: An AI search engine and the coolest speakers ever
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: “The Internet Dilemma” from Radiolab
recommendations.blurb: One of the better 30-minute summations of the Section 230 fight you’re ever going to hear, I think. It makes pretty convincing arguments for both sides, which is exactly why the fight over 230 is so messy, and it lands in about the right place.

recommendations.name: “The Doomsday AI Scenario in Hollywood from The Town
recommendations.blurb: Speaking of good pods to listen to this weekend! The Town is one of my favorite shows about the business of entertainment, and I loved this deep dive with Justine Bateman into what exactly AI might do to Hollywood. It’s a bit fatalistic in spots, I think? But it’s fascinating.

recommendations.name: Nokia G310 5G
recommendations.blurb: I don’t know if this is going to be a great phone, but it feels like an important one. It’s a nice-looking $186 midrange phone, but it’s made with user repair explicitly in mind. You can swap in more storage, a new battery, and more.

recommendations.name: The Keen utility knife
recommendations.blurb: The folks at Studio Neat have long made some of my favorite tools and accessories – the Glif phone stand lived in my bag for years — and its newest project is a small, handsome utility knife.

recommendations.name: Perplexity AI 2.0
recommendations.blurb: AI chatbots are a dime a dozen at this point, but I’ve always liked the way Perplexity handles citing its sources and delivering information — it’s a good mix of answers and links for lots of questions. The 2.0 update is basically just a redesign, but hey, it’s a good redesign!

recommendations.name: Blue Beetle
recommendations.blurb: My main goal for the weekend is to get to a theater to see Blue Beetle, which sounds like a slightly by-the-numbers but still very fun and silly superhero flick.

recommendations.name: 8BitDo Micro controller
recommendations.blurb: Trust me, a teeny-tiny game controller is exactly the smartphone accessory you need in your life. I think I still prefer the Lite model, which has joysticks, but this one is $25, weighs basically nothing, and will make all your 2D games a little more fun to play.

recommendations.name: Supreme Soundsticks
recommendations.blurb: The Harman / Kardon Soundsticks have been around for 23 years, and I think they’re still the best-looking desk speakers on the planet. I am, uh, quite confident that the Supreme collab ones will cost more than the standard $300 price for the Soundsticks 4. But that red, y’all. THAT RED.

recommendations.name: The Zen Magsafe Charger Stand
recommendations.blurb: Maisy Leigh has long been one of my favorite desk setup and productivity YouTubers, and I really dig the colorful, decidedly un-gadgety charging stand she created. Maisy’s video about the product development process is also definitely worth a watch.

recommendations.name: HyperNormalisation
recommendations.blurb: The whole Adam Curtis series of stuff, really, in terms of a modern examination of tech. HyperNormalisation is probably the gold standard.

recommendations.name: The Great Hack
recommendations.blurb: It’s a very important documentary that did its job very well. Cambridge Analytica is one of the most important stories in modern times.

recommendations.name: Lo and Behold: Reveries of the Connected World
recommendations.blurb: [Werner] Herzog’s documentary is kind of bananas. Don’t watch it expecting to come away understanding the internet better, but it’s very entertaining.

recommendations.name: Citizenfour
recommendations.blurb: Just a really, really great doc about [Edward] Snowden.

recommendations.name: Enron: The Smartest Guys in the Room
recommendations.blurb: It’s not obviously a tech doc, but it really begins to show you how companies, even if they start with the best intentions, get really off course. And how a few people can really make a bad impact on society.

recommendations.name: 2001: A Space Odyssey
recommendations.blurb: Not a documentary! But it’s, like, the great movie about algorithms being bad for you.

recommendations.name: iPhone 14 Pro Max
recommendations.blurb: The phone: iPhone 14 Pro Max

recommendations.name: Scriptable
recommendations.blurb: The widget: The Scriptable app lets you write your own iOS widgets in JavaScript.

recommendations.name: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds
recommendations.blurb: Season 2 of Star Trek: Strange New Worlds just wrapped up on Paramount Plus, and I couldn’t be more amazed that they’ve captured the spirit of the original Star Trek while making something that’s fun and modern and welcoming to viewers who didn’t grow up with Star Trek like I did.

recommendations.name: Barker & Llewelyn series
recommendations.blurb: My friend Scott McNulty recommended the Barker & Llewelyn series of mystery novels by Will Thomas, and I immediately devoured Some Danger Involved and To Kingdom Come, the first two books in that series.

recommendations.name: The Flop House podcast
recommendations.blurb: 402 episodes later, I’m still obsessed with The Flop House podcast in which two former Daily Show writers and their handsome bartender pal watch bad movies and then talk about them.

recommendations.name: The Flop House Animated
recommendations.blurb: I highly recommend The Flop House Animated for some of their greatest hits.

recommendations.name: Wanderlog
recommendations.blurb: I’ve used Tripsy in the past, but I much prefer Wanderlog because of its ability to plan a group trip while still being crossplatform.

recommendations.name: GoodLinks app
recommendations.blurb: Reading List for Safari is so disappointing. There’s no organization (folders) and you can’t tag pages you save to keep the stuff that’s similar together. I purchased the GoodLinks app and love the functionality it offers. It even has its own ‘reader’ mode like you get in Safari!

recommendations.name: Bring
recommendations.blurb: My suggestion is an app called Bring! It’s a grocery list app that allows your household to add items to a shared list, with cute little icons to boot. You can send notifications to others who are members of that list that you’re about to go shopping or that you’ve added items to the list as well.

recommendations.name: Eufy Clean G40+
recommendations.blurb: I bought a low-end robot vacuum cleaner (the Eufy Clean G40+ ) on Prime Day a few weeks ago. And as someone with very hairy cats, it’s been absolutely life-changing. I spent years thinking these gadgets weren’t any better than our old Henry Hoover, but they’re really great.

recommendations.name: Craft
recommendations.blurb: I’d like to recommend Craft. I moved to it after many (increasingly unhappy) years with Evernote, and after a bunch of months, I’m a convert. It’s got room to grow, but it’s fantastic, and I feel it doesn’t get the attention that some of the others get (like Notion and Bear).

recommendations.name: covers
recommendations.blurb: And yet, I cannot overstate how deep down the rabbit hole of “AI Taylor Swift covers of songs you know but that real Taylor Swift never covered” YouTube I have gone.

recommendations.name: songs
recommendations.blurb: Look, I get it: AI-generated songs are a massively complicated issue, with huge ramifications for both the business and the art of music.

recommendations.name: covering Lady Gaga
recommendations.blurb: It’s wild! (AI Frank Sinatra covering Lady Gaga is truly the collab of the century.) I almost don’t want to tell you how many times I’ve listened to AI Taylor Swift and AI Ed Sheeran covering Paramore’s “Misery Business.” The future is super weird, y’all.
